title: Equivalence of one- and two-function hypercontractivity
statement:
Fix a natural number $n$. Let $1 \le p \le q$ with $q \ge 2$, and let $\rho$ satisfy $0 \le \rho \le 1$ together
with $\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(q-1)}$. Then the one-function hypercontractive inequality
\[
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{T_\rho f}^q\bigr]\bigr)^{1/q} \le
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^p\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for every Boolean function } f
\]
holds if and only if the dual two-function inequality
\[
\langle f, T_\rho g\rangle \le
\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{f}^{q/(q-1)}\bigr]\bigr)^{(q-1)/q}\,\bigl(\E\bigl[\abs{g}^p\bigr]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for every pair of Boolean functions } f, g
\]
holds, where $T_\rho$ is the noise operator and $\E$ and
$\langle\,\cdot\,,\cdot\,\rangle$ are the expectation and $L^2$ inner product with
respect to the uniform measure on $\{0,1\}^n$. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
replaced:
Let $1 \le p \le q$ with $q \ge 2$, and let $0 \le \rho \le 1$ satisfy
$\rho \le \sqrt{(p-1)/(q-1)}$. Then the one-function bound
\[
  \bigl(\E[\abs{T_\rho f}^q]\bigr)^{1/q} \le \bigl(\E[\abs{f}^p]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for all } f
\]
holds if and only if the dual two-function bound
\[
  \inn{f, T_\rho g} \le \bigl(\E[\abs{f}^{q/(q-1)}]\bigr)^{(q-1)/q}\,\bigl(\E[\abs{g}^p]\bigr)^{1/p}
  \qquad \text{for all } f, g
\]
holds.
